item.title: Speed of Nepal’s Flash Floods Likely Overwhelmed Warning System, Experts Say
item.description: Scientists and disaster response researchers said Nepal’s early flood warning system relied on a conventional network of river gauges in this remote region.
item.dc:creator: Leo Sands and Binod Ghimire
item.media:description: Damage following flash floods in Trishuli, Nepal.

item.title: C.I.A. Chief Delivered Bleak Assessment of Russia’s War in Secretive Moscow Visit
item.description: John Ratcliffe’s meeting this week with a Russian intelligence chief was aimed at pushing the Kremlin to pursue a peace deal with Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: Adam Entous and Julian E. Barnes
item.media:description: John Ratcliffe, the C.I.A. director, delivered an urgent message to Aleksandr V. Bortnikov, the head of Russia’s F.S.B. intelligence service this week in a secret visit to Moscow.

item.title: Yielding on French Could Restart Trade Talks, Canadian Officials Say
item.description: Canada’s minister in charge of trade with the U.S. was responding to comments by Jamieson Greer, the U.S. trade representative. But that was before any mention of Lake Ontario.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen and Vjosa Isai
item.media:description: Dominic LeBlanc, Canada’s minister responsible for trade with the United States, center, with Prime Minister Mark Carney of Canada.

item.title: As Anger Grows Over Trump Tariffs, Some in Canada Want Out of U.S. F-35 Deal
item.description: A year into a government review of the purchase of as many as 88 F-35s, one premier says buying American warplanes makes no sense in the face of President Trump’s latest tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Ian Austen
item.media:description: The F-35 Lightning, made by American defense contractor Lockheed-Martin, costs between $82.5 million and $109 million per plane, depending on the variant.

item.title: How SSENSE, a Canadian Retailer, Is Grappling With Trump’s Tariffs
item.description: Ssense’s comeback efforts include moving a core part of its business to the United States so American customers can avoid hefty tariffs.
item.dc:creator: Peter Eavis
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: A stylist prepared a rack of clothes at a Ssense store in Montreal. The company, an online clothes retailer, is trying to lessen the burden of U.S. tariffs on its business.

item.title: Canada Hires U.S. Scholars From Harvard and Other Top Universities
item.description: A crackdown on American academia by the Trump administration has handed Canadian universities a rare opportunity to lure some top researchers north.
item.dc:creator: Vjosa Isai
item.media:credit: Nasuna Stuart-Ulin for The New York Times
item.media:description: McGill University in Montreal is one of the schools that has benefited from the Canada-bound brain drain from U.S. institutions.

item.title: On Night of Deadly Air Canada Crash, Two LaGuardia Controllers Left Early
item.description: The two controllers are among a dozen that the Federal Aviation Administration has taken steps to fire as part of an inquiry into timecard fraud, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Karoun Demirjian
item.media:credit: Dakota Santiago for The New York Times
item.media:description: An Air Canada jet crashed into a fire truck in March, killing two people.

item.title: ‘Intrinsic Capacity’: The Most Important Longevity Term You’ve Never Heard Of

item.dc:creator: Dana G. Smith

item.title: Is Haiti Safe for Haitian Deportees?
item.description: Stephen Miller said that Haiti is safe for Haitian deportees. Our White House correspondent Zolan Kanno-Youngs analyzed federal reports that say otherwise.
item.dc:creator: Zolan Kanno-Youngs, Gilad Thaler, Jon Miller, Ray Whitehouse and Stephanie Swart

item.title: Meta Projected It Could Spend $10 Billion on Anthropic’s A.I.
item.description: The social networking giant projected it could spend $10 billion annually on Anthropic’s tools, illustrating the friend-foe relationships underlying the A.I. race.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Kalley Huang

item.title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
item.description: In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.
item.dc:creator: Kate Conger
item.media:description: Sam Altman of OpenAI, which has joined more than 100 tech companies in publishing an open letter warning of a wave of cyberattacks driven by artificial intelligence.

item.title: Trump Raises Money in Texas With Control of the Senate in the Balance
item.description: Many Republicans are hoping for financial support from President Trump, whose fund-raising power in the party remains unmatched despite his low poll numbers.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Meridith Kohut for The New York Times
item.media:description: A cutout of President Trump in Cypress, Texas, during the Republican primary runoff for Senate between Attorney General Ken Paxton and Senator John Cornyn in May.

item.title: Obama to Headline Fund-Raiser With Jeffries in New York

item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher
item.media:credit: The New York Times, left, Agence France-Presse — Getty Images
item.media:description: Representative Hakeem Jeffries and former President Barack Obama will aim to give Democrats a financial boost at a time when money is a concern for the party heading into the midterm elections.

item.title: Democratic Socialists Are the Toast of the Party in Uruguay

item.title: Ratko Mladic, Murderous ‘Butcher of Bosnia,’ Dies at 83

item.category: International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia
War Crimes, Genocide and Crimes Against Humanity
item.media:description: Ratko Mladic in Sarajevo in 1994. He was captured in 2011 and put on trial for genocide and war crimes.

item.title: Jury Begins Deliberations in Lindsay Clancy Murder Trial

item.title: Roy Cohn, Robert Mapplethorpe and a Trump-Era Dilemma Over Free Speech
